## What's new in 0.1.0-beta.10
This release fixes manual searches that could hide open campsites, and moves Campertron to .NET 11. Your settings, search files and the bundled campground list keep working as they are; nothing needs to be migrated.

### Manual searches show every current match
- **Every Search shows what is open now.** With `outputTo: Console` or `outputTo: HtmlFile`, each **Search** from the menu now shows every campsite and date that matches your searches at that moment, including ones you have seen before.
- **What was wrong.** In earlier versions, HtmlFile searches and email mode recorded their results in the email notification history (the `Camp.History` folder), and later Console and HtmlFile searches then hid every campsite and date recorded there. A search could show "No entries found" or "No new matching availability to display." although the sites were still open.
- **Email history no longer affects manual searches.** Console and HtmlFile searches now neither read nor change `Camp.History`, so history left by email mode or by earlier versions no longer hides results from them.

### Email notifications work as before
- With `outputTo: Email`, Campertron still remembers in `Camp.History` what it has already emailed and doesn't email the same campsite and date again, also after a restart and also if the site is booked and later becomes free again.
- Existing history is kept exactly as it is; nothing is moved or deleted.

### Now built on .NET 11
- Campertron now runs on .NET 11. Each download still includes everything it needs, so you don't install .NET yourself. `CampertronConsole --version`, `CampertronGUI --version` and the console's View Config now show `Framework => .NET 11`.
- Campertron's database components were updated to Entity Framework Core 11 with SQLite 3.53.4.
- The Docker image now uses .NET 11 and is based on Ubuntu 26.04.
- All eight platforms and both programs (16 downloads) are still available.
- The bundled campground list is the same as in 0.1.0-beta.9. Your existing campground list (`RecreationDotOrg.db`), settings and search files work without any change.

### Processor requirements
.NET 11 raises the minimum processor only for Intel and AMD. On ARM the minimum doesn't change, but some older processors may start Campertron more slowly.
- **Intel and AMD** (`win-x64`, `win-x86`, `linux-x64`, `osx-x64` and the `linux/amd64` Docker image): the processor must now support x86-64-v2, which includes SSE4.2 and POPCNT. Practically every PC from the last decade does. On an older processor the program stops at startup with a message about missing instruction sets; keep using 0.1.0-beta.9 on such a computer. On Windows and Linux, processors without the newer x86-64-v3 features (such as AVX2) still work but may start a little more slowly.
- **Windows on ARM** (`win-arm64`): no new minimum. Most Windows on ARM PCs are unaffected. Older ARM processors, such as those in some Windows 10 IoT devices, still work but may start more slowly.
- **64-bit ARM Linux** (`linux-arm64` and the `linux/arm64` Docker image): no new minimum. Processors without the LSE extension, such as those in the Raspberry Pi 3 and 4, still work but may start more slowly.
- **32-bit ARM Linux** (`linux-arm`): no change, including Raspberry Pi computers with a 32-bit operating system.
- **Mac with Apple silicon** (`osx-arm64`): no change; every Apple silicon Mac meets the requirement.

### Consistent builds
- Some 0.1.0-beta.8 and 0.1.0-beta.9 downloads were compiled with the .NET 11 SDK's compiler although they target and include .NET 10. They run on their bundled .NET 10.0.15 like the others, and no functional difference or damage was found, so no action is needed because of this.
- From this version, every download is built with one stable .NET 11 SDK, and the release stops before anything is published if any download was compiled by a different compiler.

### Checks before publishing
The release workflow must pass all of the following before it can publish this release; if any of them fails, nothing is published:
- all automated tests, and a scan that finds no known vulnerable packages;
- every download contains .NET 11, and all 16 downloads were compiled by the same .NET 11 compiler;
- the Linux x64 console and GUI start from their downloads, and the amd64 Docker image starts;
- the checksums of all 16 downloads are generated and verified.

## Upgrading from 0.1.0-beta.9
- **Desktop:** check the processor requirements above, then extract the new archive and use it instead of your old Campertron folder. Your settings, searches, campground list and `Camp.History` (in the `CampertronConfig` data folder) are kept and need no changes.
- **Docker:** change the image tag to `0.1.0-beta.10` and recreate the container with the same `/config` and `/cache` mounts. There is no `latest` tag for beta versions, so the tag has to be changed by hand.
- **If you use email mode:** HtmlFile searches in earlier versions also wrote to `Camp.History`, so email mode treats the campsites and dates they found as already reported and won't email them. To be emailed about everything that is open again, delete the `Camp.History` folder in your settings folder while Campertron is not running.
- To check your download, use the checksums and build attestations described under "Verify your download" below.

## Known limitations
- **Windows, macOS and ARM downloads not run on real devices.** They are built and checked automatically, but only the Linux x64 programs and the amd64 container are started during the release, so the .NET 11 versions for the other platforms haven't been run yet.
- **Email clients not yet checked.** The results page was checked in Chrome and Firefox on Linux, but no test email was sent, so its appearance in Gmail, Outlook and Apple Mail is unverified. Some email programs, such as desktop Outlook, ignore much of the page's styling; the page is designed to stay readable without it. Each email contains the page twice (as the body and as the attachment), so a search with thousands of results can make a large email that some providers may reject.
- **Consecutive-night searches run together with other searches.** When several searches run at the same time and at least one of them uses `consecutiveDays`, results can still be left out, added or shown under the wrong search. If a consecutive-night search seems to be missing results, run it on its own to compare.
- **Duplicate campground names:** a small number of campground names are not unique. In those cases, the GUI may show the ID of a different campground with the same name.
- Avalonia, the GUI's UI framework, lists 32-bit Windows (`win-x86`) as a commercially supported platform only and doesn't list 32-bit ARM Linux desktops (`linux-arm`). Campertron still builds and publishes both GUI downloads, but neither is tested on a real device.
